attacks.name: Unauthorized account or system access
attacks.description: Someone logs into an account, device or system they have no right to use (credential stuffing, guessed or stolen passwords, session hijacking).
document: Date and time of each access, with time zone
Login alerts, IP addresses and device names shown by the provider
What data was viewed, changed or deleted
Proof you did not authorize the access
Any financial or other loss
caveats: Statutes require lack of authorization. A person who had your password voluntarily at the time may raise authorization as a defense.

attacks.name: Phishing and social engineering
attacks.description: Deceptive emails, texts, calls or sites that trick someone into giving up credentials, money or personal information.
document: Full message with headers (not a screenshot alone)
Links and domains used, copied as text, never clicked
What was disclosed or paid, with timestamps
Bank, card or wire records
Sender address, phone number or handle
report_to: Your bank or card issuer immediately
caveats: If money moved, contact the bank first; recall windows are short.

attacks.name: Malware, spyware or keylogger
attacks.description: Software installed without consent that records keystrokes, steals data, or damages or controls a device.
document: Name, hash or path of the file or app
How and when it likely arrived
Antivirus or forensic scan output
Behavior observed (what it captured or changed)
A preserved disk or backup image before cleanup
caveats: Preserve the device image before wiping. Cleaning the device first can destroy evidence.

attacks.name: Ransomware or cyber extortion
attacks.description: Data is encrypted, stolen or threatened with release unless payment is made.
document: Ransom note, unaltered
Wallet addresses and payment demands
Timeline of encryption or exfiltration
Systems and data affected
Whether personal information of others was taken
report_to: Virginia Attorney General if resident data was taken
caveats: If resident personal data was taken, Va. Code § 18.2-186.6 notification duties may apply to the data owner.

attacks.name: Data breach of personal information
attacks.description: Unauthorized acquisition of computerized personal information held by an organization.
document: Date breach was discovered and how
Categories of personal information involved
Number of Virginia residents affected
Whether the data was encrypted or redacted
Notification dates and recipients (affected people and Attorney General)
caveats: Va. Code § 18.2-186.6 covers specific data types (such as SSN, driver's license, financial account numbers) when unencrypted or unredacted.

attacks.name: Identity theft or impersonation
attacks.description: Using another person's identifying information or identity to gain money, credit, services, or to pose as them.
document: The impersonating account or document, captured with URL and date
Proof of your identity versus theirs
Any unlawful purpose (money, credit, harassment) the impersonation served
Platform report ID and response
Credit freeze and fraud alert records
caveats: Impersonation alone, without obtaining something or an unlawful purpose, may not meet the elements of § 18.2-186.3. Document the purpose.

attacks.name: Cyber harassment
attacks.description: Repeated abusive, vulgar, or threatening online communications meant to intimidate or harass.
document: Each message with date, time, account, and platform
Your blocks and any stop-contact request
Content of each message (copied text and screenshot)
Effect on you (distress, safety steps taken)
Platform reports and responses
report_to: Magistrate for a protective order if threats are present
caveats: § 18.2-152.7:1 turns on the content (obscene, vulgar, lewd, or threats of illegal acts) plus intent to coerce, intimidate or harass. Rude but non-obscene messages may not qualify.

attacks.name: Cyberstalking (course of conduct)
attacks.description: Repeated contact or monitoring that puts a person in reasonable fear for their safety.
document: Each act with date, time, platform and account
Proof the conduct was directed at you and continued after a block or warning
Any statements showing intent or tracking knowledge
Your reasonable fear: why the conduct frightened you
Links between accounts (writing patterns, timing, shared contacts), described as observations, not conclusions
report_to: FBI IC3 if across state lines
caveats: Va. Code § 18.2-60.3 requires conduct on more than one occasion and intent to cause fear of death, criminal sexual assault or bodily injury. Harassment alone does not satisfy it.
Linking alternate accounts to one person is an investigation question for law enforcement and platforms. Record observations; do not assert identity.

attacks.name: Threats of violence
attacks.description: Written or electronic threats to kill or injure a person or their family.
document: Exact words, unedited, with sender, date and time
Surrounding conversation for context
Why you took it seriously
Any prior violence or stalking by the sender
caveats: If you are in immediate danger, call 911 before logging anything.

attacks.name: Doxxing (publishing identifying information)
attacks.description: Posting a person's name or photo with their address or identifying information to harass or intimidate.
document: Post URL, capture date, and account that published it
What information was published (name, photo, address, ID data)
Proof the information is accurate
Evidence of intent to coerce, intimidate or harass
Takedown requests and outcomes
caveats: § 18.2-186.4 covers publication of name or photograph together with identifying information or a primary residence address with intent to coerce, intimidate or harass. A threat to dox, with nothing yet published, is analyzed under other statutes (for example, extortion or threats).

attacks.name: Non-consensual intimate images
attacks.description: Spreading or selling nude or sexually explicit images of someone to harass, coerce or intimidate them.
document: Where the image was posted, with URL and date (do not re-share it)
Who posted it and proof of intent to harass
Proof you did not consent
Takedown request IDs
If the image depicts a minor, stop and contact law enforcement; do not copy or store it
report_to: NCMEC CyberTipline if a minor is depicted
caveats: Do not store or forward intimate images, especially of minors. Record links and descriptions only.

attacks.name: Denial of service or disruption
attacks.description: Flooding or interfering with a service so legitimate users cannot use it.
document: Start and end times with time zone
Traffic logs, source IP ranges and request patterns
Downtime and business impact in dollars
Any extortion demand attached
caveats: Aggravation thresholds in § 18.2-152.4 depend on damage value and target type. Track dollar impact.

attacks.name: Block or ban evasion with alternate accounts
attacks.description: Creating new accounts to contact or monitor someone after being blocked or banned.
document: Dates of the block or ban and when each new account appeared
What each account sent or did
Writing, timing and contact-overlap patterns, described neutrally
Platform reports
caveats: Creating an alternate account is not itself a crime. It is best used as evidence of intent and course of conduct in a stalking or harassment case.

Treating a platform ban as a CFAA violation is contested: after Van Buren v. United States (2021), breaking a terms-of-service rule generally does not by itself 'exceed authorized access'. Treat § 1030 here as unsettled and ask counsel.

attacks.name: Computer-caused physical harm
attacks.description: A computer or network is used to physically injure someone, for example tampering with a connected medical device, vehicle or building control system.
document: Device or system affected, with make, model and firmware
Logs showing the unauthorized command or change
Medical or safety records of the injury
Preserved device in its current state
caveats: If anyone is in danger, call 911 first. This type is rare; § 18.2-152.7 requires that the computer use caused physical injury to an individual.
